findings.title: AAI_Animals_Tip no longer says tame undraftable animals depend on "Also while undrafted"
findings.detail: The new text says your animals "use the abilities you set to autocast". An animal that can't be drafted only autocasts undrafted: Handles needs AbilityAISettings.UndraftedAutocast for a pawn that isn't drafted, and the menu refuses it outright when that setting is off (AbilityAIAutocast.cs:217). The old tooltip said this; the new one drops it. Add a clause such as "(with 'Also while undrafted' on, unless another mod lets you draft them)".

findings.title: AAI_Approach_Tip suggests the Approach checkbox controls the player's own pawns
findings.detail: TryApproach returns early on !AbilityAISettings.Approach only for non-player pawns. The player's drafted pawns walk for "Autocast, may move" abilities whether this checkbox is on or off. The new last sentence, placed under this checkbox, reads as if it controls them. Change it to say the setting doesn't apply to your own pawns, which walk only for abilities set to "Autocast, may move".

findings.title: Walk-back paths skip CanActNowPlayer, including the Spawned check
findings.detail: TryGiveJob returns ReturnJob at the nextCastTick gate (AbilityAI.cs:849), when there are no candidates (:887) and after the candidate loop (:913), without running CanActNowPlayer. CheckHome only checks Drafted and playerForced. With ReturnToCover on, TryFindCoverCell reads pawn.Map.attackTargetsCache. A guard such as `if (!pawn.Spawned) { ClearHome(state); return; }` at the top of CheckHome would keep an unspawned pawn out of that path rather than relying on the postfix's try/catch. This is opinion: I could not show a path where a drafted pawn is unspawned.

findings.title: FightsUndrafted counts every tame animal as fighting back
findings.detail: For pawns without a configurable hostility response (UsesConfigurableHostilityResponse is colonists and colony subhumans only), FightsUndrafted returns RaceProps.Animal. So UndraftedSetNow gives a docile animal the All set whenever ctx.InCombat, which includes being hurt in the last 10 s, unless it is on a Flee job. If that is not intended, look at the animal's own flee or defend behaviour here.

findings.title: Static gizmo cache and shared instance keep the previous game's Pawn alive after a load
findings.detail: Gizmo_PsycastLimits.cachedPawn and shared.pawn are static and are only re-pointed when a pawn with psycast autocast is next selected. Loading another save leaves them holding a Pawn (and its graph) from the old Game until then. Nothing breaks, because the cache check compares by reference and the pawn changes. Clearing both in AbilityAIAutocast's constructor (where `instance` is set) would release it.

findings.title: Full is offered based on the clicked pawn only, then applied to every group-ability pawn
findings.detail: `full` checks only clicked.pawn.drafter, but the chosen mode is set for every pawn in `pawns` (groupAbility selections). A selected pawn that can't be drafted gets Full stored and behaves as Stationary. This is harmless, and the same as a Full set earlier, but the menu's claim that Full is only offered where it walks doesn't hold for mixed selections.

findings.title: Limits outlive the gizmo that sets them
findings.detail: ShouldShow hides the gizmo once no real psycast is set to autocast, but the pawn's limits entry stays stored and saved. When a psycast is set to autocast again, the old cap and floor apply without the player having seen them since. They only affect autocast, so this is a UX point and not a bug. Opinion: say in the gizmo tip that limits persist, or drop the entry when the last psycast mode goes Off.

findings.title: verify_patches' Enumerator warning does not apply to this postfix
findings.detail: verify_patches suggests MethodType.Enumerator for IEnumerable-returning Pawn.GetGizmos. The patch is a pass-through postfix (first parameter is IEnumerable<Gizmo>, returns IEnumerable<Gizmo>), which wraps the sequence lazily, the same approach as the 3 corpus mods. No change needed. The 'Not in the Schematic' line is bookkeeping.

findings.title: AAI_PlayerAutocast_Tip says "walks back to where it stood" even when Return to cover is on
findings.detail: With ReturnToCover on, MakeReturnJob sends the pawn to a covered spot within 6 tiles instead. A short "(or to nearby cover, see below)" would keep the two tooltips consistent.
